A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same repulsive score-distillation and latent–pixel augmentation framework, despite renaming RSD to RLSD and changing the paper's emphasis. The complete main texts, appendices, tables, figures, equations, and embedded animation frames support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original text-to-image, text-to-3D, Gaussian-mixture simulation, and image-inpainting results, including quantitative evaluations and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original generation and inpainting results and reports additional experiments on phase retrieval, HDR reconstruction, super-resolution, motion deblurring, and failure cases.

M1.justification: The core repulsive particle approximation and augmented latent–pixel optimization already exist in v1. v2 makes the suggested mixed strategy concrete as Hybrid-RLSD, with three interacting particles and one independent particle, and introduces interval-limited repulsion. Its published pseudocode also changes repulsion weighting and returns optimized pixel variables, whereas v1's Algorithm 2 returns decoded latents.

E1.justification: v2 adds phase retrieval, HDR reconstruction, super-resolution, and motion deblurring, substantially extending evaluation beyond inpainting. Full-face masking also adds a more difficult reconstruction scenario. FFHQ, ImageNet, text-to-image, text-to-3D, and the Gaussian-mixture example already appear in v1; the generation tasks remain in v2's appendices.

E2.justification: v2 newly evaluates Latent-DPS in Tables 3–4 and adds PSLD comparisons for ImageNet free-mask inpainting. Conversely, v1's explicit SVGD-versus-repulsion comparison, NFSD comparisons, and standalone SDS results in the supplementary trade-off plot disappear. The original inverse-problem comparators, including PSLD and pixel-domain DPS/RED-Diff, remain.

E3.justification: The reported inverse-problem backbone changes from Stable Diffusion v1.5 to v2.1, and stated regularization weights change, including half-face inpainting lambda from 0.01 to 0.14. New protocols include six-particle phase retrieval with oversampling factor 2 and restricted repulsion, and 50-image ImageNet evaluation with 500 steps. These reported setting changes do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds inverse-problem analyses of runtime/step count, repulsion strength, repulsion timing, hybrid sampling, and reconstruction failures in Appendices D.7–D.8. It removes v1's quantitative text-to-image ablations of optimization steps, particle count, guidance scale, and kernel-domain choice. The Gaussian example, qualitative kernel comparisons, and existing augmentation comparison are retained.

E5.justification: v1's Appendix C.3.2 reports aesthetic/CLIP trade-off plots with error bars, described as standard deviations in the main text. These uncertainty displays are absent from v2, although the original mean trade-off curves remain. The Gaussian experiment's 200 realizations and the identified 3D seeds are retained; no replacement uncertainty analysis is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial numerical and qualitative results for the new inverse tasks, hybrid sampling, and ImageNet evaluation, while removing several unconstrained-generation result tables and galleries. Retained comparisons also contain revised entries: pixel DPS changes from 21.35 dB/0.166 LPIPS/112.9 FID in v1 Table 7 to 23.4/0.14/78.88 in v2 Table 2. Reported setting changes limit cross-version performance attribution; random-inpainting Table 8 to Table 9 is numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The central propositions, score-matching proofs, and Wasserstein/Bures development remain. v2 revises coefficients in Proposition 2, adds conditional-posterior formulas in Appendix C and a PSLD guidance formula in Appendix B, and omits v1's reproduced ProlificDreamer theorem and NFSD formula. Appendix A.3 still retains the earlier scaling factor despite the changed Proposition 2.

C1.justification: v1 presents general repulsive score distillation for constrained and unconstrained generation, with latent inverse-problem sampling as a byproduct. v2 redefines the main contribution around jointly addressing mode collapse and latent inversion in high-resolution inverse problems. Its abstract, introduction, and conclusion foreground linear/nonlinear reconstruction and computational efficiency, with unconstrained generation becoming supporting material.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking latent reconstruction problems to decoder nonlinearity and adversarial autoencoder training, and discusses why augmentation can be unstable in phase retrieval. It interprets early repulsion as separating high-level semantics and adds specific limitations involving missing fine details, full-face reconstruction, and excessive repulsion. These materially extend v1's more general computational, kernel, and hyperparameter caveats.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands baseline-specific implementation information, pretrained-model provenance, task-specific hyperparameters, non-augmented pseudocode, and runtime documentation. It adds anonymous code-download instructions and identifies the ProlificDreamer implementation used, while retaining the original GitHub link. Some earlier generation details and timing estimates are removed.

R1.justification: The principal relationships to SDS/VSD, SVGD/CSD, RED-Diff, PSLD, and particle guidance remain. v2 expands the latent-inversion discussion with GAN-inversion references and an inverse-problem survey, adds a conceptual method-property comparison table, and removes several generation-related citations. Much of the existing particle-method discussion is relocated.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, method narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around inverse problems. The method exposition is consolidated, while score-distillation background and retained generation experiments move into reorganized appendices. This is substantial restructuring beyond the RSD-to-RLSD renaming.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the overview to expose latent–pixel augmentation, adds a method-property table, consolidates and expands the inpainting table, and adds numerous inverse-task, ablation, and failure displays. It removes several generation tables and galleries, relocates retained figures, and adds animated views of the existing 3D examples. Typography and page layout also change throughout.

improvement.justification: v1's inverse-problem claims were supported mainly by inpainting. v2 substantially strengthens their assessment through nonlinear and additional linear tasks, runtime and repulsion ablations, and explicit failure cases, including augmentation's weakness in phase retrieval. These additions clarify where the method helps and where it fails. The gains outweigh the loss of generation ablations and error bars, although the Proposition 2–Appendix A.3 scaling inconsistency remains a weakness.
